s: Pattern matching, validation, text extraction, lookaheads
d: Regex is used everywhere in backend: input validation, log parsing, URL routing, text extraction. Understanding character classes, quantifiers, capturing groups, and lookaheads makes you vastly more productive at text processing.
c: Common patterns: email, URL, IP, phone

p: Regular Expressions are sequences of characters that define a search pattern. They are extremely powerful for input validation (emails, passwords) and text parsing.
2. Define quantifiers: * (0 or more), + (1 or more), ? (0 or 1).
3. Define anchors: ^ (start of string), $ (end of string).

// Validate email format
const emailRegex = /^[\w-\.]+@([\w-]+\.)+[\w-]{2,4}$/;
if (!emailRegex.test(userEmail)) {
  throw new Error("Invalid email format");
}

Pattern: ^[A-Z][a-z]+ \d{2,4}$
Matches:
  "Alice 2023" -> YES
  "bob 23"     -> NO (must start with uppercase)
  "Carol 1"    -> NO (digit count < 2)
